what: Why the shipped upload defaults committed nothing on a policed 10 Mbit/s uplink at 100 ms (the #483 baseline), and the same workload before and after the fix: scenario 24 (the policed link, 16 x 20 MiB objects, shipped width) and the #483 harness's clean and lossy 100 ms profiles at the default configuration.

host.noise: Other work ran on the same Mac throughout and was not stopped: Docker Desktop with unrelated containers, other sessions' VMs and builds, and this change's own cargo builds and tests in Docker Desktop during some runs. None of it is separated from these numbers.

vm: Lima vz VM vtop-bench-483a (the #483 lab VM, reused): 6 vCPU, 8 GiB, Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-142-generic (ifb available), Docker 29.9.3. The only containers in it are the lab's.
lab: benchmarks/docker-compose.benchmark.yml, profiles netem + containerized; vtop-minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z, nicolaka/netshoot:v0.16, engine container ubuntu:26.04; runner_mode container, process-once.

main_937ae76.used_for: the before rows tagged main937-* (clean, lossy, and scenario 24)

fix.source: this change applied to main 937ae76 (crates/vtop-upload and crates/vtop-core changes identical to the PR's)

fix_on_b33f69f.source: the PR head: this change rebased on main b33f69f (#652), which landed while the runs above were in progress

engines.built_with: rust:latest (rustc 1.99.1) in Docker, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, cargo build --release --locked --no-default-features --bin vtopctl (the lab engine image lacks the Kafka adapter's libsasl2; the file source and s3_native path do not use it)

harnesses.scenario_24: benchmarks/run_benchmark.py from this branch with scenarios/24-policed-uplink-default-width.yaml, unchanged
harnesses.clean_and_lossy: benchmarks/egress_baseline.py (the #483 harness, since merged with #661; run from #661's branch copy in the VM), profiles wan100 and wan100-loss1, --config default, phase confirm: 16 x 20 MiB JSONL objects, compression none, one object per batch, iperf3-calibrated within +/-10% of 10 Mbit/s
harnesses.diagnostic_additions: for these runs only, the lab copy forwarded RUST_LOG into the engine container and kept every process-once stderr in full; nothing else in the harness was changed and none of it is committed

goodput: committed object bytes x 8 / the seconds of the cycle that committed them / 1e6, as egress_baseline.py computes it. The policed rows read against the policer's configured 10 Mbit/s token rate; the clean and lossy rows against that run's iperf3 calibration.
logging: RUST_LOG=info,vtop_upload=debug,vtop_cli=debug,aws_smithy_runtime::client::retries=debug,aws_smithy_runtime::client::orchestrator=debug,aws_smithy_runtime::client::timeout=debug,aws_smithy_runtime::client::http=debug; `ss -tin '( dport = :9200 )'` in the engine container's network namespace every 5 s.
